newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gencor denies calling for Mandela to quit.
newsitem.headline: Gencor denies calling for Mandela to quit.

text.p: Gencor Ltd chairman Brian Gilbertson on Friday denied a report in an Australian newspaper that he had called for the immediate resignation of South Africa's President Nelson Mandela.
"The report in the Australian Financial Review does not correctly reflect the sentiments that I tried to express to the journalist," the head of the South African mining group said in a statement.
The paper reported in its Friday edition that Gilbertson had said South Africa would benefit if Deputy President Thabo Mbeki took over now rather than in 1999, when Mandela is due to step down.
"It would be better if Mbeki could move into position and manage what has to be done now," the Financial Review quoted Gilbertson as saying.

In the statement Gilbertson said what had tried to convey was that, given the intense international interest in the succession issue and the heavy workload on Mandela, it was important that the "passing of the baton" be done smoothly.
"The timing thereof might well be better if it occurred earlier than under the political pressures of the 1999 elections," Gibertson said in the statement.
